ideas_underdeveloped.title: Developing Ideas Fully
ideas_underdeveloped.body: Underdeveloped ideas limit Task Response. For each main point, use a clear topic sentence, one concrete example, and a brief link back to the question. Aim for 2–3 sentences of explanation per supporting idea rather than listing points without depth.

position_unclear_or_inconsistent.title: Maintaining a Clear Position
position_unclear_or_inconsistent.body: Examiners expect a consistent stance throughout. State your position in the introduction, support it in body paragraphs, and restate it in the conclusion without contradicting earlier claims.

repetition_basic_lexis.title: Upgrading Repeated Vocabulary
repetition_basic_lexis.body: When the same basic words recur (good, bad, important), build a small synonym set before writing: beneficial, detrimental, significant. Use each key term once, then paraphrase with precision rather than repetition.

imprecise_word_choice.title: Choosing Precise Lexis
imprecise_word_choice.body: Imprecise words weaken Lexical Resource. Replace vague verbs (do, get, make) with specific alternatives (conduct, obtain, generate). Check collocations: 'heavy rain' not 'big rain'.

article_errors.title: Articles (a / an / the)
article_errors.body: Use 'a/an' for non-specific singular count nouns; 'the' when the reader knows which item you mean. Uncountable nouns (information, research) usually take no article.

subject_verb_agreement.title: Subject–Verb Agreement
subject_verb_agreement.body: The verb must agree with the grammatical subject, not a nearby noun. With 'the number of', use a singular verb; with 'a number of', use plural.

run_on_comma_splice.title: Fixing Run-ons and Comma Splices
run_on_comma_splice.body: Two independent clauses need a conjunction, semicolon, or full stop—not a comma alone. Example: 'Technology helps learners; it also distracts them.'
